problem:
A package of mass $500\,\text{kg}$ is released from rest and falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the package's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the package is proportional to the square of its velocity and acts in the direction opposite to its motion.
At a particular moment during the fall, the package’s velocity is $6.25\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $7.35\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Find, rounded to two decimal places, the velocity of the package after $2$ seconds.
Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the package are the weight due to gravity and drag.
worked_solution:
First, note that only two forces act on the package: the force due to gravity, given by the weight

$$
w=mg=500g
$$

and the force due to drag $D,$ which is proportional to the velocity squared (and negative since it acts in the negative direction),

$$
D=-k{v}^{2},
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality. Hence, the resultant force acting on the body is

$$
F=w+D=500g-k{v}^{2}.
$$

Applying Newton's second law, we obtain a separable first-order differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\ 500g-k{v}^{2} & =500\,\frac{dv}{dt} \\ \frac{dv}{dt} & =g-\frac{k}{500}{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that, at a particular moment, the body's velocity is $6.25\,\text{m/s}$ and its instantaneous acceleration is $7.35\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ Substituting these values and $g=9.8$ into the ODE, we can solve for $k:$

$$
7.35=g-\frac{k}{500}\cdot (6.25)^{2}\,⟹\,k=31.36\,\text{kg/m}
$$

Therefore, we have the following differential equation:

$$
\frac{dv}{dt}=g-0.06272{v}^{2}
$$

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dv}{dt} & =g(1-0.0064{v}^{2}) \\ \frac{1}{1-0.0064{v}^{2}}\cdot \frac{dv}{dt} & =g \\ \int \frac{1}{1-0.0064{v}^{2}}\cdot \frac{dv}{dt}\,dt & =g\int dt \\ \int \frac{1}{1-(0.08v)^{2}}\,dv & =g\int dt \\ \frac{1}{0.08}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(0.08v) & =gt+{C}_{1} \\ \operatorname{artanh}⁡(0.08v) & =\frac{2}{25}gt+C \\ 0.08v & =\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{2}{25}gt+C) \\ v(t) & =\frac{25}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{2}{25}gt+C)\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=0.08{C}_{1}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that the package is released from rest. So, we can apply the initial condition $v(0)=0,$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =\frac{25}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{2}{25}g\cdot 0+C) \\ 0 & =\frac{25}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(C) \\ \operatorname{tanh}⁡(C) & =0 \\ C & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $v(t):$

$$
v(t)=\frac{25}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{2}{25}gt)
$$

Finally, the velocity of the package after $t=2$ seconds is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{25}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(0.784\cdot 2) \\  & =11.4588… \\  & ≈11.46\,\text{m/s},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
